answer: Sybil resistance binds every identity to bonded collateral and uses signed histories to detect coordination. If k identities equivocate on the same decision, correlated evidence triggers pairwise slashing of O(k^2), rather than k independent penalties. Upon detection, the controller suffers a capital-loss multiplier exp(αk), while asymmetric depreciation and escrow forfeiture compound the loss. Thus a quill, vine, or grove of fabricated agents cannot cheaply spread risk.
